ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, legal representatives, direct and indirect shareholders, and UBOs against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the State Bank of Vietnam's domestic AML blacklist; enhanced customer due diligence (EDD) required for medium-risk performance advertising entities operating ISIC 7310; continuous transaction monitoring and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) status verification under Decree 19/2023/ND-CP Article 8-11.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp - dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Vietnamese company names must use Vietnamese script, digits, and the letters F, J, Z, W; names must consist of a formal enterprise type token (e.g., 'Công ty TNHH' or 'Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn') followed by a legal distinct name; Vietnamese diacritics are mandatory; foreign names may be transliterated into Vietnamese phonetic equivalents or kept in English only as the secondary dual-name; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered enterprise, must not contain abstract symbols, and must include a syllable separating the legal form from the distinctive name; 'VN' is acceptable as part of the distinctive name but the full legal name must be linguistically compliant.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Việt Nam (when used as the entire name or to imply state affiliation without approval)
International names such as 'United Nations', 'ASEAN', 'World Bank', 'European Union'
Words that violate national sovereignty, public interest, traditional culture, or require ministerial approval under Decree 108/2022/ND-CP Article 41 and Circular 01/2022/TT-BKHDT
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant receives a written notice from the Business Registration Office (BRO) of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) stating the grounds; the applicant may amend the proposed name and resubmit through the National Business Registration Portal within 30 days; if the applicant wishes to contest the rejection, it must file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the DPI within 30 days of the rejection notice (Law on Handling of Administrative Violations No. 18/2012/QH13); if the DPI Director rejects the appeal or fails to decide within 30 days, the applicant may initiate a lawsuit at the Administrative Court under the Law on Administrative Procedures and simultaneously file a formal complaint to the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI); an alternative registered name can be reserved by filing a name-reservation application using the portal and paying the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office/registered-agent-only address is not permitted for a foreign-invested limited liability company conducting performance media buying; the LLC must lease or own a physical business address located in Vietnam where the principal place of business, records, and digital operations management are situated; the address cannot be merely a postal box; however, a shared co-working space or a serviced office providing dedicated desks and legal reception is acceptable if the lease is in the company's name and invoices/receipts are available; the digital advertising affiliate model may be operated from the registered address without a physical customer-facing retail facility, but the company's server, books, and accounting records must be accessible there.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, Article 25 (enterprise registration dossiers), Article 26 (contents of application), Article 27 (time limit for issuance of Enterprise Registration Certificate), Article 28 (charter capital contribution obligations), Article 29 (legal representative), Article 74 (limited liability company with two or more members), and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration, Articles 21-39 and 46-53; for foreign investment: Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 38-40 and Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office, Agency of Business Registration, Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI); provincial Departments of Planning and Investment (DPIs) acting as one-stop-shop licensing authorities
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giay de nghi dang ky doanh nghiep) together with the Company Charter and supporting dossiers; filed online through the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum charter capital for advertising agency and digital media buying activities under ISIC 7310. Charter capital is freely declared by the founder(s). However, the charter capital must be fully contributed within 90 days from the issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate. No escrow account requirement applies to general trading and services; for foreign-invested entities, financial capacity may need to be demonstrated in the investment dossier but no escrow is imposed for non-conditional service sectors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Verify Conditional Business Lines
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn); Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the National Enterprise Registration Information System to ensure the proposed company name is legal, distinctive, and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise. Confirm that the business line 'Advertising agencies' (ISIC 7310) and 'Media buying / affiliate marketing' is not listed as a conditional business line under the Law on Investment and Decree 31/2021/ND-CP. If the name is available, proceed to reserve it or incorporate the name directly into the Enterprise Registration Application. For foreign investors, check whether an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) is required under Law on Investment Article 38; for non-conditional sectors, the ERC combines with the IRC after the investment registration process. If the proposed business scope includes advertising content production, broadcasting, or online platform services, consult with the Ministry of Information and Communications for additional notification obligations.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (Latinized Vietnamese)
Identification documents of founding members/authorized representative
Business scope description
Investment registration form (if foreign investor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, modify the name by adding distinguishing elements or changing the corporate name format, and resubmit within 10 working days. If the competent authority fails to respond within the statutory 3-working-day period, the applicant may file a written complaint to the provincial DPI or the MPI Business Registration Agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Enterprise Registration Dossier and Company Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public office (if required for legal representative authorization or lease documents); Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Company Charter, including company name, registered office, legal representative, charter capital, capital contribution timetable, capital contribution types, member rights and obligations, governance structure (sole member or board of members), decision-making rules, fiscal year, liquidation provisions, and dispute resolution mechanism. Prepare the Application for Enterprise Registration and the list of members and legal representatives. For a foreign-invested company, obtain a certified copy of the foreign investor's incorporation documents and a bank referral letter or audited financial statement evidencing financial capacity. The registered office lease agreement and the landlord's written confirmation of lawful use of the address must be signed and notarized as per local practice. Ensure all documents are translated into Vietnamese and notarized. The Charter must be signed by all founding members; the legal representative of each foreign corporate member must sign with valid authorization.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration (Form I-1 or prescribed form)
Company Charter
List of founding members and capital contributions
List of legal representatives
Copies of passports/ID cards of members and legal representative
Lease agreement for the registered office and proof of lawful use
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation (if applicable)
Financial capacity confirmation (bank letter or audited statements) for foreign investment dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is deemed incomplete, the Business Registration Office issues a written notice listing deficiencies. The applicant must remedy within 30 days from the notice date. If the company believes the rejection or deficiency notice is unlawful, it may file a complaint to the provincial DPI and subsequently to the court under administrative proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Enterprise Registration Application and Pay the Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn); Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete dossier electronically via the National Business Registration Portal. Attach digital copies of all required documents in PDF format, each with digital signatures of authorized persons. Pay the state registration fee online or at the Business Registration Office counter. After submission, monitor the dossier status on the portal. The Business Registration Office must issue or reject the Enterprise Registration Certificate within 3 working days for domestic enterprises, and within 15 working days for projects requiring investment registration, from the date of valid dossier receipt. The company may also submit by paper; the same statutory time periods apply.
required_dossiers: Electronic dossier as drafted in Step 2
Digital signature certificate of the legal representative or filing agent
Payment receipt of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal rejects the dossier due to technical errors, resubmit with corrected digital signatures. If the DPI issues a rejection, the applicant has 30 days to remedy and resubmit. A formal refusal may be appealed to the MPI or Administrative Court within 30 days of receipt of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (provincial Business Registration Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, receive the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) in electronic form, containing the enterprise code, company name, address, charter capital, legal representative, and business lines. For foreign-invested projects, also receive the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) which encapsulates the investment project. Review all entries for correctness against the submitted Charter. If the enterprise code has not been issued automatically, register for a tax identification number (TIN) with the General Department of Taxation via form 01/DK-TCT. The enterprise code is also the tax code. Announce the enterprise formation to the National Business Registration Portal as required by law.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate (issued)
Investment Registration Certificate (if applicable)
Charter and application (already filed)
Tax registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ERC contains errors or the authority fails to issue it within the statutory period, submit a written request for correction to the DPI. If the DPI refuses, the applicant may seek administrative review by the MPI or file a lawsuit at the competent administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Post-Incorporation Tax, Accounting, Seal, and Bank Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT); local tax sub-departments; State Bank of Vietnam-licensed commercial banks; DOLISA for labor registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the ERC, complete tax registration through the electronic tax portal (http://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn). Obtain the tax code confirmation. Register for VAT if annual revenue exceeds the statutory threshold or if voluntary VAT registration is desired. Affix and register the company seal (optional but recommended); the seal specimen must be declared on the National Business Registration Portal. Open a corporate bank account at a licensed Vietnamese bank or a foreign bank branch; foreign-invested companies must open a capital contribution account (Direct Investment Capital Account) as required by the State Bank of Vietnam. Register the electronic invoice system per Decree 123/2020/ND-CP. Appoint a chief accountant or retain a licensed accounting service. Register labor contracts and social insurance for employees within 30 days of commencement of operations. Publish company formation information on the National Portal if required.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Tax registration application (Form 01/DK-TCT)
Bank account opening resolution and specimen signatures
Capital contribution account certificate (for foreign-invested entities)
Company seal specimen declaration (if seal adopted)
Accounting appointment decision or service agreement
Social insurance and labor registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed due to system errors, contact the local tax authority for manual processing. If the bank refuses account opening due to insufficient documentation, provide additional corporate resolutions and legal representative ID. If penalties for late tax registration are imposed, appeal on the basis of administrative error under the Tax Administration Law No. 38/2019/QH14.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Business Commencement and Conduct Sector-Specific Compliance Review (Digital Media Buying / Affiliate Marketing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal; Ministry of Information and Communications (MIC) for cross-border advertising; Vietnam Advertising Association (self-regulatory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Announce business commencement within 30 days of ERC issuance as required by enterprise registration regulations. Review the company's digital advertising media buying operations against the Law on Advertising No. 16/2012/QH13 and Decree 181/2013/ND-CP; confirm no conditional advertising license is required for providing advertising agency services. For affiliate media buying involving online publishing and advertising networks, ensure compliance with Decree 72/2013/ND-CP on online information services and Decree 53/2022/ND-CP on cross-border information services if the company operates or accesses foreign platforms. Prepare internal policies for consumer protection, personal data protection under Decree 13/2023/ND-CP, and anti-spam regulations. If the company conducts advertising brokerage for foreign principals, verify whether any cross-border promotion license or notification applies. For all campaigns, maintain records of contractual authorizations and publisher agreements.
required_dossiers: Business commencement notice (submitted online)
Advertising service contracts/agreements with clients
Affiliate publisher agreements
Data protection policy and Privacy Policy
Internal compliance checklist for Decree 72/2013/ND-CP and Decree 53/2022/ND-CP
Power of attorney of legal representative for regulatory communications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MIC determines that certain activities are conditional, the company must suspend the activity and apply for the corresponding license. If no license requirement exists, the company may submit legal opinions to the MIC. Penalties for non-conditional activities are not applicable unless the company misstates its business scope; correct the scope by filing a change registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Industry and Trade (DoIT) at provincial level; Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT) for conditional industrial sectors; not applicable to pure advertising/media buying services under ISIC 7310
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit or manufacturing license is required for ISIC 7310 digital advertising and affiliate media buying. The activity is a non-conditional service sector. Only general enterprise registration under the Law on Enterprises and investment registration (if foreign-invested) apply. If physical offices are used, a fire safety certificate and workplace safety compliance are required separately.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) / provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category III office/service activity. Under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP and Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14, a media-buying office does not require a full Environmental Impact Assessment. If the office generates domestic wastewater only and is connected to the municipal sewer system, an environmental commitment/registration (Giay phep moi truong or cam ket bao ve moi truong) may be required depending on the local province and volume of discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For domestic wastewater discharge, comply with National Technical Regulation QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT (domestic wastewater). For office solid waste, comply with Decree 08/2022/ND-CP classification, collection, and treatment requirements. No VOC or industrial emissions apply. For electronic/e-waste from office IT equipment, comply with Circular 02/2022/TT-BTNMT on e-waste management. All discharges must be within the sewer acceptance limits of the local urban drainage enterprise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety design approval and fire safety acceptance certificate from the provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police under Law on Fire Prevention and Fighting No. 27/2001/QH10 as amended and Decree 136/2020/ND-CP. Office premises must have adequate fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, emergency lighting, and a fire safety plan. Conduct workplace risk assessment under the Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH13, including ergonomic evaluation of computer workstations, electrical safety inspections, and first-aid provisions. If the office lease is in a commercial building, ensure the building's fire safety certificate is valid and covers the leased premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế), Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Vietnam; e-Tax Portal (etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) and national e-Invoice portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV / Ngan hang Nha nuoc Viet Nam), the sole central bank and foreign exchange administration under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12 and the Law on Credit Institutions as amended, exercising FX regulatory authority through the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 05/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 (as amended by Ordinance No. 06/2013/UBTVQH13), Circular No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN on foreign exchange operations by credit institutions, and Circular No. 05/2021/TT-NHNN on lending to foreigners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam maintains a managed-floating exchange rate regime with full current-account convertibility in principle but strict capital-account controls. The Vietnamese Dong (VND) is not freely convertible offshore; all foreign-currency inflows and outflows must be settled through SBV-licensed commercial banks and reported under Balance of Payments (BoP) statistics. Current-account transactions, including cross-border media-buying service payments, advertising revenue receipts, profit dividends, interest, and royalties, are permitted without prior SBV approval provided the resident enterprise presents authentic underlying contracts, invoices, tax clearance certificates, and corporate authorizations. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI) equity contributions, offshore loans, and equity transfers, require prior registration under the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) or Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) and, where applicable, a separate foreign-loan/contribution registration with the SBV. Profit remittance by a foreign investor in an LLC is allowed once annually after the audited Vietnamese statutory financial statements are finalized and after corporate income tax (CIT) obligations are settled; no additional remittance withholding tax is imposed, but the remittance will be blocked if tax arrears or an unfiled CIT finalization exist. Practical hurdles include the requirement to open a dedicated capital contribution account, the mandatory provision of audited financial statements, local banks requiring a tax compliance certification, and documentary scrutiny designed to prevent disguised capital flight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN (Part II, Section 1) and the Law on Foreign Exchange, all export proceeds of the Viet Nam LLC for advertising and media-buying services must be repatriated into a foreign-currency account held at an SBV-licensed bank within 180 days from the date the export service is deemed completed, typically the date of customs clearance for physical goods or the contractual settlement/financial completion date for digital services. There is no fixed compulsory conversion ratio to VND under the current regulatory framework; 100% of the export proceeds must be collected and retained in a foreign-currency account, but the enterprise must sell foreign currency to the licensed bank to satisfy lawful VND-denominated obligations when required or upon request of the bank. Statutory exemptions and extensions are available only with SBV approval in cases of justified overdue receivables from non-resident trading partners, force majeure, or documented foreign insolvency proceedings. Non-compliance triggers administrative penalties under Decree No. 88/2019/ND-CP and Decree No. 86/2024/ND-CP, including fines, suspension of foreign-currency operations, and potential criminal liability for deliberate evasion in egregious cases.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal and operational feasibility rating (Low). Offshore digital EMIs such as Mercury, Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not licensed by the State Bank of Vietnam to maintain VND accounts, issue domestic payment accounts, or act as a principal clearing channel for an onshore Vietnamese corporate entity. Under Vietnamese FX and anti-money-laundering rules, all VND and foreign-currency payment transactions of a resident enterprise must be conducted through SBV-licensed credit institutions; routing primary operating cash flows through an unauthorized EMI would constitute illegal foreign-exchange intermediation and payment-services infringement under Decree No. 87/2019/ND-CP and Law on Credit Institutions. An offshore EMI may be used solely as an ancillary receivables/payables tool for settling invoices with foreign ad networks and publishers in USD or EUR, provided the Vietnamese LLC still maintains a compliant local treasury account and ensures that any onshore-to-offshore funding transfers are properly purpose-coded and documented. The principal operational treasury should therefore be a tier-1 local bank account with SWIFT/MT103 capability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vietnamese commercial banks apply the principle of in-person customer due diligence under SBV Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN on AML/CFT. The legal representative of the foreign-invested LLC — ordinarily the offshore director for a single-member LLC — must physically appear at the designated bank branch to sign account-opening documents, present original passport or national ID, certify specimen signatures, and complete a face-to-face Compliance and AML interview. Remote/fully-online account opening is not generally available to foreign directors; however, the bank may allow an onshore finance manager or a Vietnamese-appointed authorized signatory to appear with a notarized power-of-attorney legalized by a Vietnamese consulate and a board resolution from the offshore parent. Even in that case, the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must complete an identity verification call or video interview arranged by bank compliance, and the UBO's passport, source-of-funds documents, and corporate registry extract must be legalized/consularized as required. The account is activated only after the IRC, ERC, tax code certificate, seal specimen, and legitimate office documentation are verified; in practice, onboarding with physical presence takes 2 to 4 weeks, whereas remote-assisted onboarding with POA may take up to 6 to 8 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company name and declared business scope containing 'affiliate marketing' or 'digital advertising' causing automatic categorization as a high-risk business under bank internal AML risk matrices, leading to Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), prolonged review, or preliminary account rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive corporate and operational file: (1) Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); (2) a clearly written business plan explaining the affiliate media-buying model, principal platforms, advertiser networks, and geographic footprint; (3) executed master service agreements with Google Ads, Meta Business Partners, media-buying desks, and publisher networks; (4) evidence of initial share capital injection from the parent along with bank statements showing source of funds; (5) a signed office lease agreement in Viet Nam with utility bills; (6) CVs, passport copies, and reference letters for all directors/UBOs; (7) preliminary revenue and cash-flow forecasts with revenue attribution methodologies; (8) a compliance manual covering sanctions, PEP screening, and transaction-monitoring rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipation of small-ticket, high-frequency cross-border electronic payments to numerous foreign publishers and individuals in the first 90 days of operation, matching the 'money mule', 'pass-through', or 'money laundering layering' typology used by SBV Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) guidelines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A pre-approved vendor and affiliate onboarding file: (1) whitelist of partners with full corporate details and beneficial owner identification; (2) signed service-level agreements (SLAs) with each major publisher and ad network; (3) traffic delivery records, click/impression logs, and performance dashboards from the tracking platform (e.g., Redtrack/Voluum); (4) a monthly settlement reconciliation template; (5) anticipated disbursement schedule and threshold controls; (6) board resolution authorizing treasury payment limits and extraordinary approval escalation; (7) third-party independent audit or certified accountant letter describing the transaction flows; (8) documentary evidence that the company retains a proxy/attribution system proving actual performance deliverables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The offshore parent and ultimate beneficial owner residing in an AML-listed high-risk jurisdiction or having prior involvement in cryptocurrency/digital-asset trading, generating sanctions/PEP screening alerts and a request for a source-of-wealth declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured source-of-wealth file: (1) bank account statements for the past 12 months from a recognized bank in the UBO's jurisdiction; (2) source-of-wealth declaration signed by the UBO with supporting employment contracts, share purchase agreements, company formation documents, and sale-of-business deeds; (3) public registry extract and ownership structure chart for the Cayman/BVI/Hong Kong parent (if applicable); (4) negative PEP and sanctions-screening reports from each country of citizenship/residence; (5) recent notarized passport and proof of residential address; (6) a sworn affidavit that the funds originated from legitimate advertising/media operations; (7) a lawyer's legal opinion on UBO background if requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Banking transaction misclassification: applying wrong BPM6 purpose codes for service exports, e.g., labeling advertising service receipts as 'software licensing' or 'royalties,' which triggers an automatic internal red flag for trade-mismatch, misrepresentation of purpose, and potential criminal exposure under Decree No. 11/2022/ND-CP on administrative sanctions in securities and monetary areas.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A purpose-code and documentation package: (1) correct BPM6 service-code classification (e.g., code 531000 or 532900 for advertising, media, and market research) on all incoming and outgoing SWIFT instructions; (2) genuine underlying commercial agreements identifying the service provider, remuneration method, and delivery terms; (3) invoices and remittance schedules issued by the Vietnamese LLC to foreign clients and by foreign publishers to the Vietnamese LLC; (4) electronic tax invoices (hoa don dien tu) for VAT purposes on domestic supply chains; (5) transaction collar documentation showing campaign identifiers and traffic-delivery proof; (6) a copy of the FCT/CIT withholding arrangements with counterparties; (7) an audit trail document from the media-buying platform that proves the expense and revenue linkage; (8) monthly treasury reconciliation reports submitted on request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Fully compliant FDI inbound capital protocol: (1) The offshore parent contributes equity in accordance with the IRC/ERC and must post a notice of capital contribution to the SBV's Foreign Investment Administration via the local bank; (2) the LLC opens a dedicated Capital Contribution Account (Tai khoan von dau tu truc tiep) at an SBV-licensed authorized bank, denominated in USD and VND, used exclusively for inward FDI funds; (3) the parent bank originates a SWIFT MT103 wire with accurate BPM6 Balance of Payments purpose code for 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (code 5.1.1) referencing the IRC number and the Vietnamese company name; (4) the receiving bank verifies the contribution against the registered capital schedule before crediting the capital contribution ledger; (5) the LLC may then convert USD to VND at the prevailing bank TT rate for working capital; (6) quarterly ongoing reporting of disbursements and capital usage is filed with the SBV through the electronic BoP portal; (7) all transactions are subject to the 180-day rule for capital expenditure utilization as documented in the IRC; (8) no secondary foreign-currency loan is permitted without registering through a separate SBV foreign-loan file. Failure to route through the capital account invalidates the contribution for tax and licensing purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For affiliate media-buying services, outbound disbursements to foreign ad networks, publishers, and traffic sources are executed through the Vietnamese LLC's licensed bank using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (cover) for bank-to-bank settlement. Commercial Letters of Credit are not the standard instrument for service-based advertising transactions given the absence of physical goods and are generally inapplicable; documentary collections are used only for the rare tangible prepaid media trade. Each outbound payment must be accompanied by a trade-payment authorization form, the underlying service agreement and publisher invoice, a description of the transaction purpose and BPM6 code, and proof of applicable withholding tax (Foreign Contractor Tax) if the Vietnamese entity is the payer. The bank debits the FCY account, ensures the beneficiary is not OFAC/UN-sanctioned, and clears the transfer on the correspondent banking network (typically via J.P. Morgan, Bank of New York Mellon, or Standard Chartered) in USD. Domestic publisher payments in VND are settled on the National Payment Corporation of Viet Nam (NAPAS) automated clearing house or through real-time gross settlement (RTGS) within the Vietnamese interbank system. The entire payment chain must be retained for audit and be recoverable for the SBV, the Ministry of Finance, and the commercial bank's transaction-monitoring function.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/VND) with SBV-licensed credit institutions, maximum tenor of 365 days, executed against genuine commercial exposure and supporting documentation
FX swap contracts pairing a spot foreign-currency purchase with an offsetting forward sale (or vice versa), permitted between the Vietnamese LLC and its authorized bank under Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN
FX options embedded in approved hedging facilities offered by licensed banks, structured as zero-cost collars or plain-vanilla options for cash-flow protection
Natural hedging through matched foreign-currency receivables accounts and payables accounts maintained at the same licensed bank, without recourse to prohibited offshore NDFs
VND interest-rate swaps and FRA/IRS products are permissible for interest-rate risk management in conjunction with underlying borrowing, subject to bank product eligibility
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.ndf_prohibition_note: Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing VND are not permissible for domestic onshore entities under current Vietnamese FX regulations; any OTC NDF or synthetic VND position arranged offshore would be treated as a violation of the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange and Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động của doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment / Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 March, covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines from VND 10,000,000 to VND 15,000,000; failure to report for two consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off and loss of legal entity status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements of the foreign-invested enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment and Provincial Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days of the fiscal year-end (usually by 30 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or submit audited financial statements results in administrative penalties of VND 30,000,000 to VND 50,000,000 and potential refusal of tax finalization clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Finalization (Quyết toán thuế) and Corporate Income Tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department (General Department of Taxation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of VND 15,000,000 to VND 30,000,000; interest on outstanding tax at 0.03% per day; administrative arrest and compulsory tax collection for continued failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Tax Declaration and Payment (Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January, except newly established enterprises which pay within 30 days of license issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fine up to VND 10,000,000; persistent non-payment may trigger compulsory enforcement and enterprise strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises in Vietnam, including LLCs, are compulsorily subject to annual independent audit regardless of size or revenue threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) unless the enterprise voluntarily applies IFRS under permitted pilot conditions or is required by the parent group for consolidated reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not maintain a public UBO register, but AML law requires the LLC to identify, record, and maintain current beneficial ownership information. Ownership files must be updated promptly upon any member or shareholding transfer and confirmed annually during tax finalization and enterprise information reporting; failure to maintain accurate UBO data is subject to administrative sanctions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (standard Vietnamese Corporate Income Tax rate for legal entities, including foreign-invested limited liability companies; special regimes apply only to oil, gas, and rare-mineral activities at 32%-50%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and reductions: 2-year CIT exemption followed by 50% reduction for 4 years for qualifying new investment projects in eligible industrial zones; 4-year exemption followed by 50% reduction for 9 years for high-technology, software, and large-scale projects (Law No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended, Decree 218/2013/ND-CP). A VN_LLC in affiliate media buying (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810) is not in an automatic incentive sector; absent a specific investment-incentive certificate, the effective rate is the flat 20%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 01/TNDN - Provisional Corporate Income Tax Return (Tờ khai thuế TNDN tạm tính), filed electronically through the E-Tax Portal of the General Department of Taxation (etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) at the provincial tax office where the VN_LLC is registered; electronic filing requires a registered digital signature certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the end of each quarter (Q1: 30 April; Q2: 30 July; Q3: 30 October; Q4: 30 January). Aggregate provisional payments must reach at least 80% of the final annual CIT liability, otherwise the shortfall bears late-payment interest from the finalization deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number, registered name, provincial tax authority, fiscal period, and quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the LLC uses its correct Vietnamese tax code and that the address matches the Investment Registration Certificate for the media-buying business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Revenue of the quarter (Doanh thu)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover and other income earned during the cumulative quarter, excluding VAT, recognized under Vietnamese accounting standards in VND.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commission inflows from US affiliate networks settled through Mercury ACH, wire transfer, or Wise must be recognized into VND at the State Bank of Vietnam average exchange rate on the settlement date and recorded as business revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Deductible expenses (Chi phí được trừ)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable operating expenses, including media inventory purchases, sub-affiliate payouts, content production, software, labor, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to offshore related parties must satisfy the arm's-length standard of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; expenses lacking legal invoices, signed contracts, and economic substance are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Provisional CIT payable (Thuế TNDN tạm nộp)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at 20% on provisional taxable income, net of investment credits and allowable foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign owner should instruct local management to use a conservative provisional baseline so that cumulative payments never fall below 80% of the eventual final liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP escalate from VND 2,000,000 (delay up to 30 days) to VND 25,000,000 (delay over 90 days); unpaid CIT bears interest at 0.03% per day. Under-declared provisional tax can attract a 20% understatement fine or 30% if intentional concealment is established.
